channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Survey reveals rising optimism among African youth
item.description: In tonight's edition, the DRC's constitutional court approved a referendum law that critics say could open the way for President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a third term in office. Also, as the El Niño weather pattern looms, millions across Africa could face worsening droughts and floods. And a new survey suggests Africa's youth are becoming more pragmatic in how they view global powers.
item.dc:creator: Clarisse FORTUNÉ

item.title: Education minister resigns: 'Exhilarating moment' for India's youth as they demand accountability
item.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Anish Gawande, National Spokesperson for the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP). As India's younger generation challenges Modi's hardline government, Gawande frames recent government concessions, including the resignation of the Education Minister, the passage of tougher anti-cheating legislation and the appointment of a reform task force, as evidence that sustained youth mobilisation can compel accountability even within a highly centralised political system. He argues that the government's response remains fundamentally procedural rather than structural. Higher penalties and administrative reshuffling, he suggests, fail to address deeper institutional weaknesses in educational governance, technological preparedness and democratic consultation. More significantly, Gawande portrays the movement as signalling a wider political transformation: a generation that has moved beyond digital dissent into physical collective action, increasingly resistant to what he characterises as a politics of fear.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: From deer to hedgehogs: Wildfires devastate France's wildlife
item.description: As wildfires continue to tear through southwest France, thousands of wild animals are paying the price. Unable to outrun the flames or left without food and water, many have perished while others are being rescued by firefighters and volunteers.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Firefighter films wildfire using smart glasses in France's Gironde
item.description: Footage captured by a firefighter filming with his smart glasses shows his colleagues battling the blaze in the village of Le Las, in France's Gironde department, on July 27, 2026.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Trump tries to take action in the Middle East ahead of midterm elections
item.description: The US and Saudi Arabia jointly struck Iran-backed militias on July 29 in a move that widens the conflict in the Middle East. This comes a day after the US president met with the Israeli prime minister for the first time since they started their military campaign on Iran. As the midterm elections comes closer, Donald Trump is looking to take decisive action in the conflict. FRANCE 24's Angela Diffley tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'Rethink the forest' amid unprecedented wildfires: Return to 'ancestral ways of managing the land'?
item.description: Stuart Norval welcomes Jean-Luc Gleyze, President of the Departmental Council of the Gironde, and Stéphane Delpeyrat-Vincent, former firefighter and founder of WARUCENE, a research firm specialising in wildfire prevention. The Gironde wildfires expose the growing challenges of land management in a warming world. Offering complementary perspectives, Jean-Luc Gleyze, speaking from the front line of the emergency response, presents the fires as a test of social solidarity, institutional coordination, and public resilience. By contrast, Stéphane Delpeyrat-Vincent argues that increasingly destructive wildfires are not simply emergencies to be fought, but symptoms of a deeper structural failure: landscapes managed for a climate that no longer exists. Together, their analysis suggests that the challenge is no longer simply to improve firefighting capacity, but to rethink forests, communities, and urban planning in an era of accelerating climate change.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US and Saudi Araba jointly strike Iraq, widening the conflict
item.description: The US-Israel war on Iran is widening once again, with the US and Saudi Arabia launching joint airstrikes on Iran-backed armed groups in Iraq. Earlier, Tehran targeted US bases in Jordan and ships in the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump is now vowing further retaliation, raising fresh concerns that the conflict is entering a dangerous new phase.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Rescue operation at Japan shopping mall destroyed in quake
item.description: Rescuers battled through the tangled wreckage of a Japanese shopping mall Wednesday searching for any trapped survivors after a big earthquake killed at least 13 people.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Cats, dogs and horses: Rescuing the pets caught in France’s wildfires
item.description: An uncontained wildfire four times the size of Paris has forced thousands to evacuate their homes in the fire-ravaged region of Gironde in southwestern France. Many of the evacuees were forced to leave their pets behind amid the ensuing chaos. Our special correspondent in Gironde reports on the volunteers dedicated to rescuing the four-legged victims of the catastrophic wildfires.
item.dc:creator: Cyrielle CABOT

item.title: Public executions in Iran spark anti-regime protests
item.description: The Islamic Republic publicly executed two Iranian protesters in Isfahan at dawn on July 28. Several hundred people gathered near a stage set up in the city’s Alikhani Square, but instead of cheering the execution, they chanted slogans against the police, prompting anti-riot units to disperse the crowd.
item.dc:creator: Ershad ALIJANI

item.title: 'Two options' for Trump in Middle East war: 'he waits or he escalates massively'
item.description: US President Donald Trump confirmed on Fox News that the US and Saudi Arabia coordinated attacks on Iran-backed Iraqi militias with the Iraqi government itself. But Iraq has called the strikes a 'blatant violation', and its prime minister has called off a meeting with the Saudi Prince Mohammed bin Salmane due to the attack. This comes as the US struggles to put an end to the war with Iran. FRANCE 24's Angela Diffley tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Drones and bulldozers: how the army is helping battle the blaze in France's southwest
item.description: Some 1,500 French soldiers have been deployed to help combat the Gironde fire. A team of France Television reporters was granted permission to embed with some of them to see how they help support local firefighters. From widening forest trails to helping identify hotspots, potential looters or civilians trapped by the flames, they are proving useful support to firefighters.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: French wildfires: FRANCE 24 goes on the ground with firefighters
item.description: In France, the Gironde prefecture reported a second calm night and said the massive fire in the southwest was stable - but conditions are set to worsen as the country is about to be hit by a fourth heatwave, with temperatures expected to go above 40 degree celsius in the afflicted area. FRANCE 24 went with firefighters on the ground to understand what areas are considered sensitive as they battle blaze.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Comoros welcomes addition of centuries-old medinas to Unesco list
item.description: UNESCO has added six centuries–old medinas in the Comoros to its World Heritage List, drawing praise from the country's authorities as well as conservationists. Build as far back as the 12th century these ancient palaces, mosques and public squares were linked by a series of narrow streets and protected by imposing medieval walls.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Madagascar struggles to deal with wave of kidnappings hitting capital city
item.description: In Madagascar, the capital remains shaken. Since the end of June, a wave of disappearances and kidnappings has hit Antananarivo, affecting mostly children and teenagers. Last Friday, the country observed a national day of mourning for the victims. The government has announced the creation of an anti-kidnapping task force, as reports continue to come in. FRANCE 24's Aurélie Kouman met with police officers and victims' families.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Despite praise, Chad to withdraw from the International Criminal Court
item.description: Chad announced that it is withdrawing from the Rome Statute and, therefore, from the International Criminal Court, as several other countries in the Sahel region have done. In an official statement, Chad’s government criticised the ICC’s alleged partiality, arguing that most of its investigations have concerned the African continent.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: FIFA private investor plans spark backlash, UEFA fury
item.description: FIFA said Tuesday it plans to sell a stake in the business operations of the World Cup and its other competitions through the creation of a semi-private subsidiary. The decision marks a dramatic attempt to reshape the commercial landscape of global football, while opening a new front in a long-running battle with Europe for control over the massive wealth generated by the sport.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: As fires still blaze, France thinks about how to rebuild its forests
item.description: As France grapples with wildfires, President Emmanuel Macron has spoken about the steps ahead to rebuilding forests. What would this look like and what are the options available? The European Environment Agency calls for more fire-resistant vegetation and natural barriers to limit the spread. what is also crucial is allowing forests to return to a wilder state, with diverse landscapes being more resilient to fire risks.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Japan searches for earthquake survivors as thousands evacuate
item.description: After a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Japan on July 28, the country's prime minister said 13 people had died so far and many were injured. The rescue work is ongoing to find those still missing. The earthquake struck the Kumamoto area on the southern main island of Kyushu, forcing over 260,000 people to evacuate. Roads were ruptured while homes across the region saw power knocked out.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France threatens to expel Russian journalist Fedorova over alleged Kremlin propaganda
item.description: France has ordered Russian journalist Xenia Fedorova to leave the country, the interior ministry said Wednesday, amid accusations that she spread Kremlin propaganda on French television and radio. Fedorova's lawyer said she would “immediately lodge an appeal”, while her employers condemned the order as a “particularly serious breach of freedom of expression”.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: What to know about France's fourth heatwave of the year
item.description: Firefighters are worrying that strengthening winds and an incoming heatwave could reignite embers and make it harder to battle blazes in France's southwest, as temperatures are set to go above 40 degrees celsius in the area. In Paris, up to 38 degrees are expected for what is now the fourth heatwave of the year. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Firefighter 'morale remains high' despite heatwave coming to France's blazing southwest
item.description: In the southwest of France, temperatures are expected to go over 40 degree celsius just as firefighters have managed to stabilise the mass blazes in the forests of the Gironde region. They are expecting the heatwave to set fires going again but 'morale remains high', says FRANCE 24's Carys Garland, as firefighters first and foremost committed to protecting local communities.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Peru takes ultraconservative turn as Fujimori becomes president
item.description: Peru's new president Keiko Fujimori was sworn in on July 28, taking her oath of office before the country's Congress. The conservative leader now becomes the Andean nation's 9th chief executive in just 10 years - her electoral victory, an extremely narrow one - with just 50,000 votes separating her from left-wing rival Roberto Sanchez. Fujimori, wasting no time in naming her cabinet and rolling out new measures with an emphasis on fighting crime in Peru - which is facing its worst security crisis in decades.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nepal's tiger numbers rise 20 percent to an estimated 429
item.description: The number of tigers in Nepal has risen by roughly a fifth over the past four years, wildlife officials say, strengthening the Himalayan nation's reputation for conservation. But as the number of tigers in the wild has risen, the number of tiger attacks on humans has increased with it.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24
